current.text: Hachimura joined the Clippers and is projected to start at power forward, in the spot John Collins held.
Experts expect the biggest role of his career, with a usage bump as a starter. One projection has him over 30 minutes and over 18% usage, with 2 or more threes, about 16 points and 7 rebounds a game.
Brandon Ingram is injured. Bradley Beal, Jordan Miller and Konan Niederhauser are also out.
With Ingram out, Hachimura will have to take more shots.
Experts call him draftable as a late upside pick for points and threes, even though they do not like him as a player.
The Clippers' rotation is not settled. The projected starting five is not certain, Ty Lue often changes rotations, and this may be a trial season with long rotations.
The Clippers play 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. With 13 back-to-backs, they have one of the lowest totals in the league.

durable.text: He has shot over 40% from three for three straight years, but his three-point volume and usage have always been low.
Experts rate him a very good to elite three-point shooter who should take more threes.
He shoots a good field goal percentage, around 51% to 54% in recent seasons.
He gives almost nothing in assists, steals and blocks.
He rarely gets to the free throw line and is not a good free throw shooter.
He is a consistent shooter with a pull-up midrange game. He is not much of a creator and not a good defender.
Experts do not see him as a good fantasy player. He is compared to Harrison Barnes: threes on low usage and little else.

note: He is a 1 USD or end-of-draft pick. Yahoo ranks him 121 and ESPN ranks him 197, which puts him near the edge of our 144-player pool. His projected line (51.7% FG on 8.8 attempts, 1.6 threes, 0.6 turnovers) gives a small lift in FG% and TO. He gives little in AST, STL and BLK, so he suits teams that already get those categories elsewhere. Check his early minutes and three-point attempts while Ingram is out: over 30 minutes and about 2 threes a game would make him a solid starter, and anything less makes him a waiver-level player.
